# Trove
> File sharing service. Upload any file, get a shareable link.

## API

Set `TROVE_BASE_URL` to your Trove deployment:

    export TROVE_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8080"

### User attribution
Send X-Trove-User-Email on every API or agent request so both reads and writes
are attributed. It is required for POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE requests. Trove
uses the email for audit attribution only; it does not grant access.

### Upload a file
POST /upload
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

Parameters:
- file (required): The file to upload (.html, .md, .zip, images, code, etc.)
- slug (optional): Custom URL slug (lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, 1-64 chars)
- overwrite (optional): Set to "true" to replace an existing file at the same slug
- if_match (optional, recommended when updating): the version you last read.
  The upload replaces the artifact only if it is still at that version;
  otherwise it returns 412 with current_version and changes nothing. Implies
  overwrite. An If-Match header works too.

Headers:
- X-Trove-User-Email (required for writes): Email used for audit attribution.
  Trove's browser UI prompts once, caches the email locally, and sends this
  header automatically. API and agent clients must provide it explicitly on
  every request.
- X-Trove-Client (optional): your tool and version, e.g. trove-skill/1.3.0.
  Trove tells you when a newer version is available.

Response (JSON):
- url: The shareable URL for the uploaded file
- slug: The slug assigned to the file
- type: "site" when a ZIP was uploaded as a multi-page website
- version: the stored version; send it as if_match on your next update
- hints: suggestions for a better link preview (missing title, summary,
  stats or preview card) and client updates. Act on them before sharing.

Before you upload HTML or Markdown that people will share, give it a
preview: a title, a one- or two-sentence summary that states the takeaway,
the key numbers as stats, and for reports, proposals and dashboards a
preview card. See "Make links preview well" and "Set a preview card".

Example (single file):

    curl -X POST "$TROVE_BASE_URL/upload" \
      -H "X-Trove-User-Email: you@example.com" \
      -F file=@report.html -F slug=my-report

Example (multi-page website from ZIP):

    zip -r site.zip my-site/
    curl -X POST "$TROVE_BASE_URL/upload" \
      -H "X-Trove-User-Email: you@example.com" \
      -F file=@site.zip -F slug=my-site

### Update an existing artifact safely
Someone else (or another agent) may have changed it since you last looked.
Read the current version, merge their changes into yours, then upload with
if_match:

    curl -s "$TROVE_BASE_URL/api/artifacts/my-report"   # {"version": "...", ...}
    curl -X POST "$TROVE_BASE_URL/upload" \
      -H "X-Trove-User-Email: you@example.com" \
      -F file=@report.html -F slug=my-report -F if_match=<version>

On 412, fetch /my-report/raw, merge, and retry with the new version. For
ZIP sites the check happens before writing (not atomically) and sites
uploaded before versions existed have an empty version: overwrite them once
without if_match to get one.

### Get artifact metadata
GET /api/artifacts/{slug}
Returns slug, kind (file or site), version, content_type, filename,
owner_email, file_count (sites) and url, without the content. /{slug}/raw
also sends the version as its ETag.

### Upload a multi-page website
Upload a ZIP file containing an index.html at the root. Trove serves it as a full
multi-page website — relative links between pages and assets work automatically.
A single top-level directory inside the ZIP is stripped automatically.

Requirements:
- ZIP must contain index.html at the root (or inside a single top-level directory)
- All pages and assets (CSS, JS, images) should use relative paths

### View a file
GET /{slug}
Returns an HTML page that renders the file (markdown, code, images, CSV, HTML, etc.)
For multi-page sites, returns the site viewer with index.html loaded in an iframe.

### Navigate a multi-page site page
GET /{slug}?page=path/to/page.html
Loads a specific page within an uploaded multi-page site. The URL updates as you
navigate, so any page can be linked or shared directly.

### Serve a site asset
GET /{slug}/{path}
Returns a raw file from within an uploaded multi-page site (HTML, CSS, JS, images).

### Download raw file
GET /{slug}/raw
Returns the raw file content with its original content type (single-file uploads only).

## Comments

Every Trove viewer supports persistent, collapsible comment threads, including
files that were uploaded before comments were introduced. A root comment may
apply to the whole file, an element, or selected text. Threads support replies,
editing, deletion, resolution, reopening, and viewing resolved threads. The
browser viewer provides the comment UI; API and agent clients can use the
endpoints directly.

The supplied email is manually asserted audit attribution, not verified
authentication. Trove compares it to the original author email before allowing
edit or delete, but that comparison is an ownership convenience rather than a
security boundary. Any identified writer can reply, resolve, or reopen.

### List comment threads
GET /api/artifacts/{slug}/comments

Query parameters:
- path (optional): Current page path inside a multi-page site, such as
  index.html or reports/summary.html. The response includes threads for that
  page plus whole-artifact threads.
- resolved (optional): open (default), include, or only.

Headers:
- X-Trove-User-Email: Send on reads when available for audit attribution.

Response:
- threads: Newest-first array. Each item contains root and oldest-first replies.
- open_thread_count: Number of open threads in the response.
- current_version: Storage version of the current file or site page.
- resource: Normalized multi-page site path, when applicable.

Example:

    curl "$TROVE_BASE_URL/api/artifacts/my-report/comments" \
      -H "X-Trove-User-Email: you@example.com"

Link to a thread with `/{slug}?comment={thread_id}` (add `&page={path}` for a
site page): the viewer opens the comments sidebar on that thread.

### Create a comment thread
POST /api/artifacts/{slug}/comments
Content-Type: application/json

Headers:
- X-Trove-User-Email (required): The server uses this as the comment author.
  Do not put author_email in the JSON body.

Anchor types:
- file: Whole-file or whole-page comment.
- element: HTML or rendered-view element, identified by stable_id or selector.
- text: Highlighted text, identified by quote.exact and optional surrounding
  quote.prefix and quote.suffix.

Whole-file example:

    curl -X POST "$TROVE_BASE_URL/api/artifacts/my-report/comments" \
      -H "X-Trove-User-Email: you@example.com" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"body":"Please add the source date.","anchor":{"type":"file"}}'

HTML element example:

    curl -X POST "$TROVE_BASE_URL/api/artifacts/my-report/comments" \
      -H "X-Trove-User-Email: you@example.com" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"body":"Make this chart larger.","anchor":{"type":"element","stable_id":"revenue-chart","selector":"[data-trove-id=\"revenue-chart\"]","label":"Revenue chart"}}'

Multi-page site comments include the page in anchor.resource:

    {"body":"Clarify this heading.","anchor":{"type":"text","resource":"reports/summary.html","quote":{"exact":"Quarterly summary","prefix":"Results — ","suffix":" for FY26"}}}

The response root contains id and thread_id. Use the root id for replies and
thread resolution.

### Reply to a thread
POST /api/artifacts/{slug}/comments/{root_comment_id}/replies
Content-Type: application/json

For a multi-page site, also send path as a query parameter.

    curl -X POST "$TROVE_BASE_URL/api/artifacts/my-report/comments/$ROOT_ID/replies" \
      -H "X-Trove-User-Email: you@example.com" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"body":"Updated the chart source."}'

Replies are rejected while a thread is resolved. Reopen it first.

### Edit a comment or reply
PATCH /api/artifacts/{slug}/comments/{comment_id}
Content-Type: application/json

The X-Trove-User-Email value must match the comment's original author email.

    curl -X PATCH "$TROVE_BASE_URL/api/artifacts/my-report/comments/$COMMENT_ID" \
      -H "X-Trove-User-Email: you@example.com" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"body":"Corrected comment text."}'

### Delete a comment or reply
DELETE /api/artifacts/{slug}/comments/{comment_id}

The X-Trove-User-Email value must match the original author email. Deleting a
root with replies leaves a body-free tombstone so the replies remain threaded;
an empty deleted thread disappears.

### Resolve or reopen a thread
PATCH /api/artifacts/{slug}/comments/{root_comment_id}/resolution
Content-Type: application/json

Any identified writer may resolve or reopen:

    curl -X PATCH "$TROVE_BASE_URL/api/artifacts/my-report/comments/$ROOT_ID/resolution" \
      -H "X-Trove-User-Email: you@example.com" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"resolved":true}'

Use false to reopen. List with resolved=include or resolved=only to view
resolved threads.

### Author HTML with durable comment anchors

No special markup is required: Trove falls back to semantic labels and CSS
selectors, so existing HTML is immediately commentable. For anchors that
survive recurring overwrites, add stable metadata to meaningful components and
text regions:

    <section
      data-trove-id="revenue-chart"
      data-trove-label="Quarterly revenue chart">
      ...
    </section>

Rules:
- data-trove-id must be unique within one page.
- Keep the same data-trove-id when regenerating or overwriting the artifact.
- Put IDs on meaningful components or text regions, not every nested span.
- data-trove-label is optional human-readable context shown in the drawer.
- Add data-trove-comment-ignore to transient chrome or controls that should not
  be selectable.
- Semantic HTML, ordinary id attributes, labels, ARIA labels, headings, and
  visible text improve fallback anchors.

### Make links preview well

When a Trove link is posted in Slack, the preview is built from the artifact
itself. Always set these when you author a page; the upload response lists
any that are missing.

HTML pages:

    <title>Q3 Marketplace Review</title>
    <meta name="description" content="Q3 beat plan on GMV; three bets for Q4.">
    <meta name="trove:stat" content="GMV: $48.2M (+12% vs plan)">
    <meta name="trove:stat" content="Orders: 412k">
    <h2>Headline numbers</h2> ... <h2>Q4 bets</h2>

- Title: og:title, then <title>, then the first <h1>.
- Summary: meta description (or og:description); otherwise the first
  paragraph of 40+ characters outside nav/header/footer. One or two sentences
  that state the conclusion work best.
- Stats: up to six trove:stat meta tags, each "Label: Value", shown as a grid.
- Contents: the <h2> headings, in order (up to six).
- Multi-page sites use the entry page.

Markdown:

    ---
    title: Checkout p99 regression postmortem
    description: p99 doubled for 40 minutes after a cache config change; no failed orders.
    stats:
      - "Duration: 40 min"
      - "Failed orders: 0"
    ---

- Without frontmatter: the first "# " heading is the title and the first
  prose paragraph is the summary.
- "## " headings become the contents list; reading time and mermaid diagram
  counts are added automatically.

CSV previews show the header and first rows; code and text show the first
lines; JSON shows top-level keys. Flagged artifacts preview as title only.
Where guests are present, or Trove can't see who's in the conversation (DMs),
the person who shared the link is asked before a preview is posted.

### Set a preview card (optional image)

For a richer Slack preview, render a compact image yourself (for example a
small HTML card with the title and one key chart, screenshotted with a
headless browser) and attach it. The card replaces the excerpt and contents
line; the title, summary, stats and comment details still show.

    curl -X PUT https://trove.example.com/api/artifacts/q3-review/preview \
      -H "X-Trove-User-Email: you@example.com" \
      -F "image=@card.png" \
      -F "alt=Q3 GMV vs plan by week"

    chrome --headless --hide-scrollbars --window-size=1200,630 \
      --screenshot=card.png card.html

- PNG or JPEG, 100–2000 px per side, up to 2 MB; 1200x630 is recommended.
  Keep text large: Slack shows it small.
- Re-upload to replace; DELETE the same URL to go back to the text preview.
  Overwriting the artifact keeps the card.
- GET returns the stored image. Cards are not shown for flagged artifacts or
  for previews the sharer chose to show as title only.
- Previews fall back in order: card image, then the tags above, then content
  Trove derives from the file.

### Agent metadata
GET /.well-known/agent.json
Returns structured JSON metadata for agent integration.
